For our execs and compliance team we need:
- A snapshot of runtime artifacts (traces, request IDs, sample request/response metadata) around the incident window
- A statement of what will be redacted and confirmation that no customer PII is being shared
- Chain-of-custody / integrity checks for any file you share (checksums, manifest)
- ETA — their CTO expects something within 6 hours or they'll escalate to procurement/legal.

Please let me know the minimum we can provide immediately and the mechanism for secure transfer. If you need a non-disclosure or specific delivery controls (KMS key), tell us now.

Thanks,

Aditya / Monica — urgent. Aureum is asking for incident artifacts and chain-of-custody details; they want an ETA within 6 hours. Key questions: what sanitized artifacts can we produce quickly that are useful to their SREs but avoid exposing prompt text or PII?

My proposal:
- Generate a time-bound snapshot (07:50-08:10 UTC) with: request IDs, trace spans (no full prompt text), top-level response codes, token counts per request, worker IDs hashed, and sampling of request headers.
- Produce a manifest.csv with sha256 checksums for each file.
- Deliver via a signed S3 URL (expires in 72h) with server-side encryption; if they require use of a customer KMS key we'll coordinate legal.

Can you confirm:
1) Who will run the snapshot (Aditya?) and how long to produce?
2) What redaction steps will run (PrIyom / Markus to confirm policy)?
3) Any objections from Security to delivering the manifest and hashed identifiers?

Attaching their screenshot for context.

Short answer: we can deliver a sanitized snapshot and manifest within ~3.5-4 hours if we prioritize. Details and constraints below.

What we'll include (sanitized):
- traces.tar.gz: compressed traces with all prompt/text fields removed, request_id, span timestamps, status_code, model_variant, token_count, and an anonymized worker_id (HMAC with per-tenant salt).
- metrics.csv: minute-resolution latency/error aggregates and sample histograms.
- manifest.csv: filename, sha256, generation-timestamp.

Redaction policy: strip any prompt or response text that contains strings matching our PII patterns (SSNs, account numbers, full names followed by account ids). Keep header metadata (user-agent, geo) at top level only. If a sampled request contains business-sensitive SQL or exec commands we will exclude that sample and note exclusion in manifest.

Chain-of-custody: we will generate SHA256 checksums and a signed Manifest (signed with our internal signing key). Delivery: signed S3 pre-signed link, SSE-KMS. If Aureum requires BYOK (their KMS) we need legal approval — that will add time.

Action owners:
- Aditya: run snapshot and package (ETA 3 hours)
- Monica: coordinate CS comms and redact PII exceptions (ETA 4 hours)
- Priyom: confirm legal / policy language for manifest and sign-off (ETA 2 hours)

Attachments: audit-manifest-template.csv (use this as the manifest format).

Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Reliability & Security | Redwood Inference

Sara — quick update and plan of record.

We can provide a secured, sanitized snapshot covering 07:50–08:10 UTC. Package will include: traces.tar.gz (no prompt/body text), metrics.csv, and manifest.csv with SHA256 checksums. Redwood will hash worker IDs (HMAC) and exclude any samples that match our PII filters — we will list exclusions in the manifest.

Delivery method: pre-signed S3 URL (SSE-KMS). If Aureum requires us to encrypt to your KMS, please confirm the KMS ARN now; otherwise we'll use our standard SSE-KMS key and provide the signed link.

Timeline: Aditya will produce the snapshot and Monica will run redaction verification. We expect delivery in ~4 hours from now (by ~15:45 UTC). Priyom will send a short attestation describing redaction steps and the chain-of-custody.

We will not include any prompt or complete response text in the snapshot. If your auditors require additional granularity (e.g., full request logs under a legal process), let us know and we can escalate to legal/procurement.

ETA and link will be provided once the package is generated.
